rows.requirement: Price-snapshot store that records opening and closing numbers for every market we originate
rows.what_exists: Schema, an empty snapshot table (0 rows) and a validator that refuses unverified prices.
rows.gap: The committed feed holds one closing-type value per market (spread_line, total_line, moneylines, spread and total odds) and no opening value or capture time. Nothing can be back-filled from it, so the opening-vs-closing comparison is blocked.
rows.source_label: committed feed, 7,548 rows (repo file; columns read on 2026-11-14)

rows.requirement: Verified results feed so backtests and ROI can be computed
rows.what_exists: A results feed with one game verified against NFL.com: 2026 Week 10, Washington 24 at New York Giants 21 (Thu 12 Nov, Final).
rows.gap: The committed nflverse snapshot shows this game with blank scores, so it is stale for Week 10. Every other game is unverified against an official page, so backtests and ROI cannot be computed yet.

rows.requirement: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline
rows.what_exists: The origination module's docstring lists the outputs as spread, total, then moneyline. The brief's 'side' is read as the spread.
rows.gap: No gate checks the order of origination or stores it per row. The snapshot schema carries origination_order (1 spread, 2 total, 3 moneyline) so the order can be enforced once data exists.

rows.requirement: Publish the model's fair line, the market line, and the difference as separate columns
rows.what_exists: The origination board publishes own_spread, mkt_spread and edge_spread as separate columns (and the same pattern for the total and the moneyline).
rows.gap: The board is the 2026-11-01 Week 8 snapshot, not the current slate. Its market columns carry no capture time, so they cannot be tied to an opening or closing snapshot.
rows.verified: column names yes; market values not checked against a sportsbook

rows.requirement: Separate 'signal' from 'staking' in the leaderboard so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal
rows.status: partial · gate built, leaderboard not yet using it
rows.what_exists: A demotion gate that judges signal (closing-line value) and reports staking (ROI) separately, with tests showing a lucky staking run cannot keep a bad signal live.
rows.gap: The published leaderboard still ranks by gates passed and then by ROI, so the staking metric is part of the ordering. No live strategy exists to evaluate.

rows.requirement: Track the depth of the replacement, not just the fact of a replacement
rows.status: partial · injuries tracked, depth order blocked
rows.what_exists: Injury report rows are tracked per team and slot (review-board/data/injuries.json). The depth page exists.
rows.gap: The official report says who is out but not who replaces them, and no official depth order is in the verified data. The depth page therefore leaves both replacement columns blank on every row, so the depth of a replacement (starter / 2nd / 3rd / 4th string) cannot yet be measured.
rows.verified: blanks verified; no depth order published

rows.requirement: Compute correlations only from officially sourced numbers and publish n with each value
rows.what_exists: Correlations are published with n (for example home vs away points, n = 7,087 games).
rows.gap: Every input comes from nflverse, which is a third-party extract, not the league. Under the official-only rule the set is empty: 1 verified game (R2) is too few for any correlation.

rows.requirement: Define a demotion gate that sends a live strategy back to paper
rows.what_exists: A pure-function gate with three outcomes (HOLD, KEEP_LIVE, DEMOTE_TO_PAPER) and nine passing unit tests on synthetic fixtures.
rows.gap: Thresholds (200 settled bets, one-sided 95%) and the use of closing-line value as the signal are PROPOSED. They are not from an official source and have not been validated on real results. No live strategy exists yet.
rows.verified: code and tests yes; thresholds are proposals
